title: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursive Self-Improvement
mutable_substrate: Live Python agent code in runtime memory, including the downstream task policy, the self-referential learning/update algorithm, and potentially the available action set; the constrained experiments do not update foundation-model weights.
optimization_operator: An LLM decision function inspects the current runtime, validation feedback, history, and high-level goal, then generates monkey patches that add, replace, or remove policy and optimizer logic. Recursion makes each patched controller govern subsequent updates.
feedback_selection: Task-specific validation utility supplies scores and low-performing examples. The live agent reasons over feedback, evaluates patched policies, changes direction, or reverts to a previous best; updates are empirical rather than proof-certified.
archive_memory: One live canonical code state plus growing historical context of analyses, evaluations, errors, and prior decisions. The agent can revert to previous optimal logic, but no explicit population or diversity archive of independent lineages is described.
validation_strategy: Six independent cycles per task, each capped at 30 recursive iterations. DROP, MGSM, and MMLU use 128 validation and 800 held-out test questions; GPQA uses 32 validation and 166 test questions with five evaluations. Results report 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.
adaptation_mode: Validation-time offline self-optimization through live runtime rewriting, followed by held-out inference with the optimized policy. The discussion frames code rewriting as executable test-time compute.
principal_results: Gödel Agent-base scores 80.9 +/- 0.8 on DROP, 64.2 +/- 3.4 on MGSM, 70.9 +/- 3.1 on MMLU, and 34.9 +/- 3.3 on GPQA, versus Meta Agent Search at 79.4, 53.4, 69.6, and 34.6 respectively.

The no-constraints variant scores 90.5 on DROP, 90.6 on MGSM, 87.9 on MMLU, and 55.7 on GPQA, primarily because it may request help from stronger models such as GPT-4o and is not an equal-model comparison.
Across 100 MGSM optimization trials, 92% contain temporary performance drops, 4% terminate unexpectedly, and 14% finish worse than the initial policy.
On Game of 24, one trajectory replaces an LLM Chain-of-Thought solver with recursive symbolic search after six unsuccessful updates and reaches 100% accuracy.
A 30-step process across the four main domains is reported to cost about $15 versus $300 for Meta Agent Search.
Random GPT-4o policy samples remain around 30% MGSM accuracy, while the feedback-driven trajectory recovers from bad patches and finishes around 63%.
limitations: Updates are not proof-certified and can temporarily regress, finish below baseline, or destroy the recursion mechanism.
The agent may lose self-comprehension as its rewritten code grows more complex; the transition point is unmeasured.
Small repeatedly queried validation sets create adaptive overfitting risk.
The positive comparison uses a stronger GPT-4o optimizer to synthesize policies evaluated with GPT-3.5 and imports baseline scores from prior work.
The unrestricted condition can call stronger models and is not directly comparable with closed-book GPT-3.5 systems.
The system follows one live lineage and has no explicit diversity archive.
Cost claims lack a complete token, pricing, and repeated-cycle breakdown and depend on dated proprietary endpoints.
The study does not compare directly with heavily engineered production-scale agents.
safety_controls: Runtime error handling carries exceptions into the next step and supports backtracking or reversion.
Held-out test sets separate policy-selection feedback from final evaluation.
The ethics section recommends sandboxed execution and explicit constraints on permissible modifications.

The experimental goal prompt grants unrestricted code, environment, library-installation, and external-LLM privileges, so sandboxing and constrained modification are recommendations rather than demonstrated non-bypassable controls.
Editing the recovery or recursive-improvement code remains a known unprotected failure mode.

explicit_predecessors.name: Gödel machine
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The framework explicitly adopts self-reference and recursive code modification from the Gödel machine while replacing proof search with LLM planning and empirical validation.

explicit_predecessors.name: Self-Taught Optimizer (STOP)
explicit_predecessors.evidence: The related-work section identifies STOP as applying recursive self-improvement to code generation with the optimizer itself as the target; Gödel Agent expands the mutable state to policy, learner, and actions.

explicit_predecessors.name: Meta Agent Search
explicit_predecessors.evidence: Gödel Agent is evaluated against Meta Agent Search and argues that its own update algorithm can change rather than remain a fixed human-designed search routine.

explicit_predecessors.name: Chain-of-Thought and self-consistent Chain-of-Thought
explicit_predecessors.relationship: Initial policy and repeatedly rediscovered policy component
explicit_predecessors.evidence: All main tasks begin from Chain-of-Thought, and the learned benchmark policies commonly add multiple samples, roles, verification, and voting.

open_questions: Can empirical self-rewriting obtain monotonic or probabilistic improvement guarantees without reverting to a completely fixed optimizer?
How can recursive and recovery modules be protected while still allowing meaningful self-improvement of the optimizer itself?
At what code complexity does the underlying LLM lose the ability to accurately model and safely modify the full agent?
How much of the reported gain survives larger validation sets, distribution shift, modern open models, and fully reproduced baselines?
Can population archives, branching lineages, or transactional patches improve diversity and recovery at acceptable cost?
What forgetting or compression policy reduces growing historical-memory cost without discarding information needed to diagnose and revert failures?
How should model access, library installation, filesystem, network, secrets, and budgets be enforced outside mutable agent code?
Do multi-agent Gödel systems converge to cooperation, specialization, competition, or evaluator manipulation?
What changes when the agent is allowed to fine-tune the LLM as well as rewrite its scaffolding?
